gloss: to want; to desire (showing signs of)

definitions.gloss: to want; to show signs of wanting
definitions.explanation: Used to describe when someone (usually a third person) displays behavior indicating they want something.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもがおもちゃを{欲|ほ}しがっている。
{彼女|かのじょ}はいつも{新|あたら}しい{服|ふく}を{欲|ほ}しがる。
{人|ひと}の{持|も}っているものを{欲|ほ}しがるのはよくない。
examples.english: It's not good to covet what others have.

notes:
VERB TYPE:
{他動詞|たどうし} (transitive verb)

CONJUGATION:
Godan verb ({五段動詞|ごだんどうし}) ending in る
・{欲|ほ}しがらない (negative)
・{欲|ほ}しがって (te-form)
・{欲|ほ}しがった (past)

GRAMMAR NOTE:
This is the -がる form of the i-adjective {欲|ほ}しい. The -がる suffix converts adjectives describing internal feelings into verbs that describe observable behavior. It is typically used for third persons, as Japanese speakers generally don't claim to observe their own feelings from outside.

{欲|ほ}しい vs {欲|ほ}しがる:
・{欲|ほ}しい - I want (1st person, direct)
・{欲|ほ}しがる - (someone) wants, shows signs of wanting (3rd person, observed)

OTHER -がる VERBS:
・{怖|こわ}がる - to be afraid (from {怖|こわ}い)
・{恥|は}ずかしがる - to be shy (from {恥|は}ずかしい)
・{寂|さび}しがる - to feel lonely (from {寂|さび}しい)
・{嫌|いや}がる - to dislike (from {嫌|いや})
